To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the error performance of reliability based decoding algorithms is governed by the distribution of the minimum distance of the code, and that the error performance analysis can be reduced to the study of the probability of error of an equivalent binary symmetric channel.

for the GMD decoding algorithm, the error probability of the GMD decoding can be bounded from above by the sum of the probability of decoding errors and the probability of undecodable words, where the former is upper bounded by the probability of the union of events that correspond to decoding errors, and the latter is upper bounded by a term that is the product of the probability of the event of undecodable word, and the probability of the intersection of the event of decoding errors and its complement, and
for any reliability-based decoding algorithm, the probability of error can be expressed in terms of the reliability function, which can be computed by a simple iterative procedure.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the error performance of all these decoding algorithms is very close, and that the best one depends on the code and the decoding radius.
the GMD decoding is not the best decoding algorithm in terms of error performance, and the Chase-type algorithm is the best one in most of the cases.

the statistical approach proposed by Agrawal and Vardy (2000) is a very powerful tool to analyze the error performance of reliability based decoding algorithms, which has not been exploited to its full potential.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the statistical approach is very powerful in analyzing the error performance of reliability-based decoding algorithms, and it is a very good complement to the union bound approach.
the error performance of reliability-based decoding algorithms can be evaluated in a unified way by the statistical approach proposed by Agrawal and Vardy.

for the GMD decoding, the bound proposed by Agrawal and Vardy (2000) is the most accurate one; for Chase-type, combined and ordered statistic decodings, the bound proposed in this paper is the most accurate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the error probability for a given code and decoder is a function only of the code rate and not of the code size.
the error performance of reliability-based decoding algorithms can be analyzed by using a simple and unified framework based on the statistical approach of D. Agrawall
the error performance of reliability-based decoders can be analyzed by considering the probability of decoding error as a function of the number of decoding steps.
